claims.text: Applying high-strain compressive loading during sintering can reduce the effective sintering temperature of high-entropy alloy powders.
High-strain compression promotes a clustering-to-ordering transition.
The compression-induced transition facilitates atomic rearrangement and bond formation at lower temperatures.
As-atomized Al0.1CrCoFeNi powders are typically disordered or partially clustered.
Compression should be applied during the early stages of sintering.
The proposed intervention can operate near or below a spinodal temperature of approximately 840 K.
The molecular-dynamics study used a very high deformation strain rate.
Practical experimental strain rates would be lower than those used in the molecular-dynamics study.
Compression enhances unlike-pair correlations such as Al-Co and Al-Cr.
Tensile loading produces clustering without a clustering-to-ordering transition.
Compression-induced ordering lowers the energy barrier for particle bonding and densification.
Compression will permit densification at a lower processing temperature than conventional sintering without compression.
Compression-assisted low-temperature sintering may improve mechanical integrity.
Conventional sintering without high-strain compression requires higher-temperature thermal activation for densification and ordering.
The proposed effect may be limited by experimentally achievable strain rates and may depend on alloy composition and initial microstructure.
Translating the molecular-dynamics result to powder sintering is uncertain because of differences in strain rate, scale, and powder-processing complexity.

contradictions.description: The design compares a compression-loaded sample at reduced temperature with a conventional sample at the typical temperature, but the rule treats similar densification as evidence of no temperature reduction. Achieving similar densification at the lower temperature would instead support the claimed reduction unless temperature is varied systematically to determine the minimum temperature for each condition.
